title: IRGC Launches Second Night of Retaliation — Missiles/Drones at Ahmad Al-Jaber AB, Residential Fire in Kuwait City
detail: Early Sept 3 (Day 189), Iran's Artesh launched a second consecutive night of missile-and-drone retaliation, claiming strikes on satellite-communications systems, equipment warehouses, and fighter-aircraft hangars at Ahmad Al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait. Kuwait's General Staff said air defenses were 'responding to hostile missile and drone threats'; Kuwait's fire brigade said a drone strike sparked a fire at a residential complex in Kuwait City, causing material damage but no casualties. Kuwait's foreign ministry called the attacks 'a grave breach of the rules of international law.' JINSA counted at least 59 missiles/drones fired at Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraq over Sept 1-2 alone — the largest single barrage since the April 8 ceasefire — with this Sept 3 wave following as a second round.

confidenceReason: Iran claims specific damage to satcom/warehouses/hangars at Ahmad Al-Jaber AB; a US defense official told media the strikes 'did not impact any US bases.' Only the Kuwait City residential fire is independently confirmed (by Kuwait's fire brigade), with no casualties.

title: Iran's First VP Aref Warns of 'Asymmetric,' 'Multi-Layered' Response, Says US Should 'Stockpile Gasoline'
detail: Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said on Sept 3 that the US strikes of the past week have permanently changed Tehran's 'security equations and defense doctrine,' warning that Iran's future response will be 'asymmetric,' 'multi-layered,' and 'security-depriving for the aggressor.' Writing on X, Aref added: 'The Americans should start thinking about stockpiling gasoline and fuel. Dark months await the American economy' — a reference to the Strait of Hormuz blockade's effect on global fuel supply.
